facts.statement: Courseware highlights company-charge registration but states a broad 30-plus-300-day route; that timing statement is held back pending version-specific primary comparison.

facts.locator: sections 77–80, PDF pp. 64–65; cover date 1 September 2026; section 77 proviso footnote effective 2 November 2018
facts.statement: Section 77 distinguishes 30-day registration duty and conditional late routes by charge-creation regime; later registration cannot prejudice intervening rights. Registration certificate is separately required for section 77(3) treatment by liquidator/other creditor, while section 77(4) preserves repayment obligation. Section 78 provides a chargeholder application route; section 80 addresses deemed notice. This post-cutoff consolidation is not itself evidence of the whole June 2026 regime.

payload.title: A signed charge and a registered charge are different file stages
payload.core_explanation_md:
For a company security, keep creation evidence, the applicable filing duty, actual registration and the certificate distinct. Section 77 addresses registration with the Registrar and a certificate following registration. A signed hypothecation agreement alone is not evidence that the statutory registration step is complete.

The inspected section also separates treatment of the charge by the liquidator or another creditor from the underlying repayment obligation. Section 77(3) sets its registration/certificate condition; section 77(4) preserves the repayment contract or obligation. Do not translate a filing failure into an assertion that the borrower automatically owes nothing. Other registries and applicable law may impose additional requirements.

self_check.prompt_text: Can a missing charge-registration certificate alone justify saying that the repayment obligation is extinguished?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. Section 77(4) preserves the repayment contract/obligation despite the section 77(3) qualification.

payload.title: Use the right creation-date regime before quoting a deadline
payload.core_explanation_md:
The courseware broad extension statement should not be applied to every new company charge. The inspected section 77 provisos distinguish creation regimes and make late-registration routes conditional on application and the prescribed fees. Subsequent registration also cannot prejudice a right acquired before actual registration.

The retained consolidation is dated **1 September 2026**, after this exam cutoff. Relevant footnotes point to earlier amendments, but a release reviewer must still verify the June 2026 provision and rules. This draft therefore assesses the need to identify the correct regime, not a real filing deadline. Section 78 separately permits the specified chargeholder application where the company fails to register; assuming only the company can ever act also misses a statutory route.

self_check.prompt_text: Why is a September 2026 consolidation insufficient by itself to certify every June 2026 filing rule?
self_check.expected_takeaway: The source date is after the exam cutoff; the applicable provision and subordinate-rule versions need verification.

payload.stem_md: A company has not completed charge registration. A lender concludes that the underlying repayment contract is automatically cancelled. Which inspected provision distinguishes those issues?

options.text_md: Section 80 makes every unregistered charge equivalent to a registered one
options.explanation_md: The deemed-notice rule does not supply missing registration or erase the section 77 conditions.

options.text_md: Section 77 requires the borrower to pay nothing whenever filing is delayed
options.explanation_md: That conclusion conflicts with the express preservation of repayment obligations.

options.text_md: The loan interest rate decides whether registration is needed
options.explanation_md: Pricing is not a substitute for examining the statutory charge-registration requirements.

options.text_md: Section 77(4) preserves repayment obligations despite the section 77(3) charge-treatment qualification
options.explanation_md: Registration treatment and the repayment obligation are expressly distinguished.

payload.correct_explanation_md: Registration treatment and the repayment obligation are expressly distinguished.

options.explanation_md: Another unsupported universal date would not resolve the version and conditions problem.

options.text_md: Verify the applicable creation-date regime and June 2026 provision/rules before calculating a filing deadline
options.explanation_md: The inspected text distinguishes regimes and conditions, while the retained consolidation postdates the cutoff.

options.text_md: Assume a post-cutoff document date proves every rule was already in force at cutoff
options.explanation_md: The document date alone does not establish earlier applicability.

options.text_md: Treat the signed security agreement as proof of both registration and certificate issue
options.explanation_md: These are separate statutory and evidentiary stages.
